title: Incident orchestration playbook: three-tier probes and investigation playlist
content:
Purpose:
This is a working-level playbook for incident orchestration focused on three-tier probes (micro, cohort, canary) and an "investigation playlist" template operators can run during production anomalies. The goal is to give SREs and operators a compact set of probes, hypotheses, and dashboard annotation rules to speed MTTI/MTTR and reduce noisy alerts.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies primarily to tokenized text generation, embedding serving, and KV-prefetch/caching layers.
- Assumes existing trace context propagation across frontend -> router -> model-serving -> kv-cache -> storage.
- Designed to be runnable from the operator runbook UI (console quickcards) and via CLI snippets included below.

Three-tier probe taxonomy (short):
1) Micro probe (fast, cheap, per-host):
   - Purpose: detect host-level regressions (GPU kernel stalls, OOMs, disk latency).
   - Frequency: every 30s - 2m, lightweight synthetic token requests (short prompts).
   - Key metrics surfaced: per-host p95 TTF token, qps concurrency, gpu-allocator-frees/sec, local-kv-hit-rate.

2) Cohort probe (customer-like workload):
   - Purpose: validate end-to-end quality and latency for high-impact tenant cohorts.
   - Frequency: configurable (1m - 5m) and tenant-weighted.
   - Requests: sampled production prompt set (anonymized), include embedding + generation paths if used.
   - Key metrics: cohort p50/p95 latency, hallucination score proxy (embedding cosine drift), response-size tokens, prefix-warmth.

3) Canary probe (release/rollout oriented):
   - Purpose: detect regressions introduced by model or infra rollouts before wider exposure.
   - Frequency: high cadence during rollout (every 10-30s), tied to rollout campaign.
   - Key metrics: canary pass-rate, semantic-fidelity checks, model-variant latency delta compared to baseline.

Probe design knobs and instrumentation checklist:
- Correlate probe traces with tenant and route tags (tenant_id, route, model_version).
- Always attach kv-cache-warmth and kv-eviction-reason tags to responses spawned from cached prefix paths.
- Include a short embedding fingerprint (first 8 chars of sha1 of normalized prompt) for cohort probes to map regressions to prompt families without revealing PII.
- Measure and emit: request_received_ts, queue_enter_ts, backend_start_ts, kv_lookup_ts, model_decode_start_ts, model_decode_end_ts, response_sent_ts.

Trace naming and span conventions (operator-friendly):
- Root span: "request.{tenant}.{route}"
- Router span: "router.lookup_route" (tags: route, region)
- KV span: "kv.lookup" (tags: cache_hit:boolean, warmth:int, eviction_reason)
- Model span: "model.decode" (tags: model_name, model_variant, seq_len, quantization)
- Postprocess span: "postprocess.rerank" or "postprocess.format"
- Sampling rules: prefer including full traces for canary and cohort probes; micro probes can use 1-in-10 full traces, 1-in-2 minimal spans.

Trace sampling matrix (recommended starting points):
- Canary probe: 100% traces with full span retention and payload annotations for first 30m of rollout.
- Cohort probe: 30% full traces, 100% minimal spans (timings + tags).
- Production traffic: adaptive 2% full traces with severity-weighted upscaling (if latency > p95 baseline then sample 100% of that tenant's requests for 5m).
- Embedding-heavy routes: increase full trace sample multiplier x2 for first 24h after model change.

Dashboard and annotation conventions:
- Panel naming: <layer> / <signal> — e.g., "kv-cache / warmth-index (tenant)" or "model-decode / p95 latency (seq<=512)".
- Time-slice annotations: when an operator runs a replay or a mitigation (scale-up), add annotations with action, owner, and ticket-id. Standard format: "[ops] <action> — <owner> — <ticket>" (console quickcard will auto-emit).
- Pin the three probes into a single compact dashboard tile group titled "Incident leash: probes" with small sparklines and green/yellow/red thresholds derived from SLOs.
- Dashboard widgets: keep max 6 metrics per incident tile; prefer ratio metrics (errors per 1k requests) and latency quantiles.

SLO derivation heuristics for probe signals (examples):
- Backend p95 token-latency SLO for model-decode: baseline 200ms -> set alert threshold at baseline * 1.6 for yellow, baseline * 2.5 for red.
- KV hit-rate SLO: target 98% for warm cohorts; alert if < 94% sustained for 5m.
- Canary fidelity pass-rate: minimum 99% pass across templated assertions; alert on sustained drop > 0.5% absolute.

Investigation playlist (operator template) — run in order until hypothesis validated or mitigated:
1) Quick triage (1-3 min):
   - Check "Incident leash: probes" tile: which tier is failing? micro/cohort/canary?
   - Look at recent dashboard annotations and rollout events.
   - Run: curl to probe endpoint using --header "x-playbook-debug: yes" and compare timing headers (response contains timestamps). CLI snippet:
     - curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $RUNBOOK_TOKEN" -H "x-playbook-debug: yes" "https://api.redwood.ai/probe?prompt=short-test" -D -

2) Trace dive (5-15 min):
   - If micro probe shows host-level noise: filter traces by host_id, inspect gpu-allocator-frees and disk-read-latency spans.
   - If cohort probe failing: group traces by embedding-fingerprint and compare model.decode.seq_len distributions.
   - Helpful queries: "service:model-decode AND tag:model_variant=canary AND duration>200ms" in trace search.

3) Hypothesis runs (10-30 min):
   - Hyp 1: KV cold-start / eviction storm — check kv.eviction_rate and set a temporary cache-size bump for the affected pool.
      Action: patch autoscaler config, annotate dashboard: "[ops] bump-kv-size — Priya — ENG-8673".
   - Hyp 2: Model kernel regression — swap traffic to baseline variant (fail open) and observe canary pass-rate rollback.
   - Hyp 3: Traffic spike/backpressure — throttle low-priority tenants and measure queue_enter_ts drop.

4) Mitigation and follow-up (post-resolve):
   - Create retro note with prompt fingerprints that triggered cohort failures (anonymized).
   - Add permanent probe for the failing fingerprint family into cohort set.
   - Fill short incident postmortem template: root cause, detection signal, time to mitigation, follow-ups.

Operator quickcards (one-line actions for console):
- "Capture traces for tenant X for 10m": increases trace sample multiplier x10 for tenant X for 10m.
- "Roll model X -> baseline": initiate immediate rollback to baseline model variant with canary halt.
- "Warm KV pool <pool-id>": trigger synthetic batch warming (10 requests) for pool.

Dashboard ergonomics suggestions for this playbook:
- Single-line severity badges (green/yellow/red) based on precomputed composite score across three probes.
- Compact probe tile should expose the last-failed-probe-reason and trace link (one-click).
- Make the probe group collapsible to preserve vertical space on the incident page.
- Add quick links to runbook templates and CLI snippets inline in the dashboard.

Example queries & snippets (for immediate copy/paste):
- Minimal trace filter for cohort failures:
  service:model-decode AND tag:embedding_fingerprint=abcd1234 AND duration>150ms | sort by duration desc | limit 50
- KV eviction spike timeseries (promql-like):
  sum(rate(kv_evictions_total{pool="prefetch"}[1m])) by (pool)
- Quick probe curl with debug headers:
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $RUNBOOK_TOKEN" -H "x-playbook-debug: yes" -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/internal/probe/run" -d '{"probe":"cohort-alpha"}'

Known limitations and TODOs:
- We currently do not correlate embedding drift signals with ground-truth customer labels; plan: add offline evaluation hook to cohort probe within 2 sprints.
- Tracing payload redaction needs an automated sanitizer for prompt snippets; until then, all cohort probes use hashing-based fingerprinting.
- Need an operator-visible cost estimator before enabling high-rate canary full-trace retention.

Appendix: short glossary (operator language)
- Warmth: heuristic 0-100 for cache usefulness for a tenant (higher = more warm).
- Canary pass-rate: fraction of canary probes that pass a semantic assertion harness per unit time.
- Embedding fingerprint: hashed, truncated prompt representation used to bucket similar prompts without storing raw text.

Notes / next steps:
- Schedule a 60m lab to prototype the passive-to-active sampling escalation rule described in Trace sampling matrix. Owner: Evan Chung; due: 2026-01-22.
- Add runbook quickcard to console for "bump-kv-size" that includes rollback TTL.

End of playbook (working draft).
